title: Cycles and boundaries for a filtered complex
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex, and let $F^\bullet K^\bullet$ be a finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. For every $p,q,r$ with $r\ge1$, define subobjects of $\operatorname{gr}^pK^{p+q}$ by $Z_r^{p,q}=((F^pK^{p+q}\cap d^{-1}(F^{p+r}K^{p+q+1}))+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})/F^{p+1}K^{p+q}$ and $B_r^{p,q}=((F^pK^{p+q}\cap d(F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1}))+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})/F^{p+1}K^{p+q}$. Then $B_r\subseteq Z_r$ and the filtered-complex spectral sequence has $E_r^{p,q}\cong Z_r^{p,q}/B_r^{p,q}$. Equivalently, writing $X^{[a,b]}=F^aK^\bullet/F^bK^\bullet$, the same object is naturally isomorphic to the image of $H^{p+q}(X^{[p,p+r]})\to H^{p+q}(X^{[p-r+1,p+1]})$ induced by the map $F^pK^\bullet/F^{p+r}K^\bullet\to F^{p-r+1}K^\bullet/F^{p+1}K^\bullet$. For $r=1$, $Z_1$ is the cycles of $\operatorname{gr}^pK$ and $B_1$ is its boundaries, so $E_1=H(\operatorname{gr}^pK)$; for sufficiently large $r$ the terms stabilize. This is the filtered-complex description of Stacks Tag 012K.

source.place: Homology, Lemma 12.19.2, label lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex, Tag 012K (cycle and boundary description)

proof.text: Use the filtered-complex construction [lem-sp-filtered-complex-associated-spectral-sequence-construction]. Its graded differential object has component $F^{p+1}K^{p+1+q}$ and its injective shift map is induced by $F^{p+1}K^{p+1+q}\hookrightarrow F^pK^{p+1+q}$; hence the resulting page differentials have bidegree $(r,1-r)$ and its initial graded object is $\operatorname{gr}^pK^{p+q}$.

source.place: Definition 12.18.1 and Remark 12.18.2, applied in the proof of Lemma 12.19.2 (Tag 012K)

proof.text: Unwinding the kernel and image formulas for the self-map spectral sequence gives, in the component of total degree $p+q$, $Z_r^{p,q}=((F^pK^{p+q}\cap d^{-1}(F^{p+r}K^{p+q+1}))+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})/F^{p+1}K^{p+q}$ and $B_r^{p,q}=((F^pK^{p+q}\cap d(F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1}))+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})/F^{p+1}K^{p+q}$. The inclusion $B_r^{p,q}\subseteq Z_r^{p,q}$ follows because $d^2=0$ and $d(F^{p-r+1})\subseteq F^{p-r+1}$, while the page definition is $E_r^{p,q}=Z_r^{p,q}/B_r^{p,q}$.

For the equivalent cohomology description (working with elements in the abelian category, as in Stacks), write $\tilde Z=F^pK^{p+q}\cap d^{-1}(F^{p+r}K^{p+q+1})$. Every class in ^{p+q}(F^pK/F^{p+r}K)$ is represented by some \in\tilde Z$, and since \ge1$ we have \in F^{p+r}\subseteq F^{p+1}$, so the same $ is a cocycle of ^{p-r+1}K/F^{p+1}K$ representing the image class. Hence the image is the quotient of $\tilde Z$ by $\tilde Z\cap(d(F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1})+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})$. If =dy+f$ with \in F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1}$ and \in F^{p+1}K^{p+q}$, then =x-f\in F^pK^{p+q}\cap d(F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1})$; conversely every element of ^pK^{p+q}\cap d(F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1})$ lies in $\tilde Z$ because ^2=0$. So this kernel is $\tilde Z\cap((F^pK^{p+q}\cap d(F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1}))+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})$, and the map $\tilde Z\to Z_r^{p,q}/B_r^{p,q}$, which is surjective by the definition of ^{p,q}$, has exactly this kernel. Thus the image is naturally ^{p,q}/B_r^{p,q}$.

source.place: Lemma 12.19.2, cycle-boundary formulas and quotient-complex interpretation, Tag 012K

proof.text: At $r=1$, the condition $d^{-1}(F^{p+1})$ is the kernel of the differential on $\operatorname{gr}^pK$, and $d(F^p)$ gives its boundaries, so $Z_1$ and $B_1$ are the cycles and boundaries and $E_1=H(\operatorname{gr}^pK)$. Since the filtration is bounded degreewise, for fixed $p,q$ both tails $F^{p+r}K^{p+q+1}$ and $F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1}$ are eventually zero or equal to the relevant endpoint; the displayed subobjects therefore stabilize for sufficiently large $r$.
